answer: Agents can gate reputation behind a slowly accumulated, nontransferable stake: each identity must lock scarce tokens and earn trust through repeated, independently verified work before it can influence routing or rewards. A newcomer may mirror a trusted agent’s history, but the copied record does not transfer with the stake. To forge many credible identities, an attacker must fund each one and keep them active long enough to build evidence; they cannot cheaply wander in, claim influence, and disappear without risking locked capital.
